summary: Today’s pulse tracks Nvidia dismisses 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign as Trump backs effort to reinstate ex CEO, Trump defends commerce secretary Lutnick for allegedly slow-walking Nvidia chip export restrictions – live, and Freeman Johnson, oldest survivor of Pearl Harbor attack, dies aged 106. Across BBC, Guardian, and NPR, the strongest repeated signals are attack, california, and waves. In the background, California braces for more towering waves as powerful storms approach and California sues OpenAI over hacking risks keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Nvidia dismisses 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign as Trump backs effort to reinstate ex CEO
headlines.description: A number of tech figures have backed an effort asking the AI chip giant to give Jensen Huang his job back.

headlines.title: Trump defends commerce secretary Lutnick for allegedly slow-walking Nvidia chip export restrictions – live
headlines.description: President backs Lutnick after treasury secretary Scott Bessent blamed commerce department for delays in blocking advance AI chip exports

headlines.title: Freeman Johnson, oldest survivor of Pearl Harbor attack, dies aged 106
headlines.description: Johnson was working on the USS St Louis and was inside a steam drum when the attacks took place The oldest known survivor of the Pearl Harbor attack died Saturday aged 106 years old. Freeman Johnson, a fireman below the deck during the attack, died in his home in Massachusetts, according to the Boston Globe . Only 11 known Pearl Harbor survivors are still living, all of whom are centenarians.

headlines.title: California braces for more towering waves as powerful storms approach
headlines.description: NWS issues advisories for long stretches of the northern California coast, warning that waves can quickly overpower anyone nearby The massive, 50-foot swells along California’s coast this weekend foretold an intense week of towering waves to come. Officials from the National Weather Service (NWS) had issued advisories for long stretches of the California coast, warning people that erratic and unpredictable waves could quickly overpower anyone nearby. The highest waves – which reached 50 to 60ft (15.24 to 18.29 meters) – cracked along the popular Mavericks surf spot in San Mateo county, south of San Francisco.

headlines.title: California sues OpenAI over hacking risks
headlines.description: The state's attorney general started investigating OpenAI after the Hugging Face attack and now says this attack was "entirely foreseeable" due to OpenAI's poor security practices.

headlines.title: Customers report difficulty accessing online services at major US banks
headlines.description: Bank of America, Chase, US Bank, Wells Fargo and Truist were listed by users who have been experiencing issues Customers reported service outages and difficulty accessing their online accounts at several major US banks and the money transfer service Zelle on Monday after a technical issue at JPMorgan Chase caused ripple effects throughout the financial system. Chase said the technical problems were not a systemic issue and were not the result of a cyber-attack, and that it was working to bring banking services back online.

headlinePool.title: California sues OpenAI over safety concerns after rogue agent hacking
headlinePool.description: The lawsuit stems from an earlier incident where the tech company’s products hacked into the open-source platform Hugging Face California sued OpenAI on Monday, accusing the artificial intelligence titan of developing its technology without safety or the public’s interest in mind. The lawsuit concerns an incident earlier this year where OpenAI agents – semi-autonomous AI software that can carry out digital actions on behalf of users – launched a cyber-attack into the open-source AI platform Hugging Face.

headlinePool.title: Houthi rebel advance in Yemen may further destabilise global economy
headlinePool.description: The Iran-backed Houthis are gaining ground and their advance could have dangerous consequences, writes the BBC's security correspondent.

headlinePool.title: Third US aircraft carrier brings thousands more troops to Middle East
headlinePool.description: The US president oscillates between strike threats on Iran and insisting the war ‘militarily is effectively over’ A third US aircraft carrier has arrived in the Middle East, US Central Command said in a social media post on Monday, making a dramatic show of military might as Donald Trump keeps his options open for next steps in the Iran war. The USS Theodore Roosevelt brings thousands of additional troops to the Middle East as Trump has oscillated between threatening additional large-scale strikes on Iran and insisting that the more than eight-month-old war “militarily is effectively over”.

headlinePool.title: Albanese signs on to Trump’s AI supply chain pact before leaders’ meeting at Quad summit
headlinePool.description: Quad leaders’ summit in Philippines is Trump’s first, as Australia joins US and Japan to protect AI technologies in face of China’s efforts to dominate The Quad leaders’ summit in the Philippines’ capital of Manila will be Trump’s first, in either of his presidencies. The US president, fresh from a crushing midterms result, will take centre stage in gatherings of Asian leaders and prepare for historic three-way talks with Xi Jinping of China and Russia’s Vladimir Putin this week.
